title: A History of the Inquisition of the Middle Ages
author: Henry Charles Lea
query: History of the Inquisition of the Middle Ages Lea
epithet: The great documentary history of the medieval Inquisition
summary: Lea's three-volume history, built directly from the archives, of the medieval Inquisition and its pursuit of heresy, sorcery and magic — the founding monument of the critical study of persecution.

title: Materials Toward a History of Witchcraft
author: Henry Charles Lea
query: Materials Toward a History of Witchcraft Lea
epithet: The archival dossier a lifetime assembled
summary: The vast collection of sources on witchcraft and its prosecution that Lea gathered over decades — the raw material of the subject, indispensable to every later historian of the witch trials.

title: A History of Witchcraft in England from 1558 to 1718
author: Wallace Notestein
query: History of Witchcraft in England Notestein
epithet: The first archival history of the English trials
summary: Notestein's careful history of English witchcraft prosecution from Elizabeth to the last trials — the first study grounded in the assize records rather than the pamphlets, and long the standard.

title: Witchcraft in Old and New England
author: George Lyman Kittredge
query: Witchcraft in Old and New England Kittredge
epithet: The folklore beneath the witch trials
summary: Kittredge's learned study setting the English and New England witch beliefs in the long tradition of popular magic — the book that reframed witchcraft as folklore rather than mere delusion.

title: The Witch-Persecutions
author: George Lincoln Burr
query: The Witch-Persecutions Burr
epithet: A documentary reader of the great hunts
summary: Burr's collection of translated source-documents of the European witch persecutions — a compact reader that put the words of the trials themselves before the student for the first time.

title: Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds
author: Charles Mackay
query: Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds Mackay
epithet: Alchemists, prophets and the crowd's follies
summary: Mackay's classic survey of mass delusion — alchemists, fortune-tellers, the Crusades of prophecy, the witch mania and the tulip bubble — the ancestor of every sceptical history of the irrational.
imprint: London: Office of the National Illustrated Library, 1852

title: A History of the Warfare of Science with Theology in Christendom
author: Andrew Dickson White
query: Warfare of Science with Theology White
epithet: The long quarrel of science and the churches
summary: White's two-volume account of the conflicts of science and dogma — astrology, alchemy, demonology and magic among them — the book that fixed the 'warfare' model of science and religion.

title: A History of Magic and Experimental Science, vol. I
author: Lynn Thorndike
query: History of Magic and Experimental Science Thorndike volume 1 first thirteen
epithet: The first two volumes: antiquity to the thirteenth century
summary: The opening volume of Thorndike's monumental history, tracing the entanglement of magic and natural science from the Roman Empire through the early Middle Ages — the foundation of the whole field.

title: Folk-Lore in the Old Testament
author: James George Frazer
query: Folk-Lore in the Old Testament Frazer
epithet: The comparative method turned on Scripture
summary: Frazer's three volumes reading the narratives of the Hebrew Bible against the folklore and custom of the world — the comparative anthropology of The Golden Bough applied to Genesis and beyond.

title: Researches into the Early History of Mankind
author: E. B. Tylor
query: Researches into the Early History of Mankind Tylor
epithet: The making of the science of culture
summary: Tylor's earlier book, working out the comparative method — myth, gesture, fire-making, magic — that he would crown in Primitive Culture; a founding text of anthropology.

title: The Making of Religion
author: Andrew Lang
query: The Making of Religion Andrew Lang
epithet: Where anthropology met the séance
summary: Lang's argument that the reports of psychical research and the beliefs of 'savages' about visions and spirits deserved the same serious study — an anthropology of religion that took the uncanny seriously.

title: Magic and Religion
author: Andrew Lang
query: Magic and Religion Andrew Lang
epithet: Lang's quarrel with The Golden Bough
summary: Lang's collection attacking Frazer's sharp division of magic from religion and defending the antiquity of belief in a high god — a key document in the great debate over the origins of religion.

title: The Threshold of Religion
author: R. R. Marett
query: The Threshold of Religion Marett
epithet: Awe before the gods: the theory of mana
summary: Marett's essays proposing a 'pre-animistic' stage of religion rooted in awe and the sense of impersonal power — mana — a decisive refinement of Tylor's account of the origins of the sacred.

title: Lectures on the Religion of the Semites
author: William Robertson Smith
query: Lectures on the Religion of the Semites Robertson Smith
epithet: Sacrifice and the origins of the sacred
summary: Robertson Smith's lectures on sacrifice, taboo and the sacred among the ancient Semites — the work that shaped Frazer, Durkheim and Freud and founded the sociological study of religion.

title: The Elementary Forms of the Religious Life
author: Émile Durkheim
query: Elementary Forms of the Religious Life Durkheim
epithet: Religion as the society worshipping itself
summary: Durkheim's study of totemism as the elementary form of religion, arguing that the sacred is society representing itself to itself — a founding classic of the sociology and theory of religion.

title: From Ritual to Romance
author: Jessie L. Weston
query: From Ritual to Romance Weston
epithet: The Grail as a fertility mystery
summary: Weston's argument that the Grail legend preserves the ritual of an ancient fertility mystery — the study, out of the Frazerian school, that shaped modern readings of the Grail and inspired The Waste Land.

title: The Mystic Rose
author: Ernest Crawley
query: The Mystic Rose Crawley marriage primitive
epithet: A study of taboo, marriage and the primitive sacred
summary: Crawley's study of the taboos and rites surrounding sex and marriage among 'primitive' peoples — an influential attempt to ground religion and magic in the anxieties of the body.

title: Orpheus: A History of Religions
author: Salomon Reinach
query: Orpheus History of Religions Reinach
epithet: A rationalist's universal history of religion
summary: Reinach's compact, sceptical history of the religions of the world — taboo, totemism and the survival of magic among them — a widely translated handbook of the comparative study of religion.

title: Demonology and Devil-Lore
author: Moncure Daniel Conway
query: Demonology and Devil-Lore Conway
epithet: A natural history of the world's demons
summary: Conway's two-volume comparative survey of demons and the Devil across the world's mythologies — an ambitious Victorian attempt to trace the natural history of the idea of evil.

title: The History of the Devil and the Idea of Evil
author: Paul Carus
query: History of the Devil and the Idea of Evil Carus
epithet: The Devil from Egypt to the modern world
summary: Carus's richly illustrated history of the figure of the Devil and the problem of evil across cultures — a monist philosopher's survey that became a standard popular reference.

title: The Geography of Witchcraft
author: Montague Summers
query: The Geography of Witchcraft Summers
epithet: A believing scholar's map of the witch-cult
summary: Summers's country-by-country survey of witchcraft in Europe — learned, credulous and written by a man who insisted the witches were real — a strange and much-cited companion to his History.

title: The Vampire: His Kith and Kin
author: Montague Summers
query: The Vampire His Kith and Kin Summers
epithet: The first scholarly history of the vampire
summary: Summers's learned, lurid study of the vampire in folklore, theology and literature — the founding work of vampire scholarship, gathering the whole tradition into one credulous volume.

title: The Book of Were-Wolves
author: Sabine Baring-Gould
query: The Book of Were-Wolves Baring-Gould
epithet: The lore and cases of the man-wolf
summary: Baring-Gould's pioneering study of lycanthropy in folklore, history and psychology — the first English book on the werewolf, and a source-quarry for every later treatment.

title: Curious Myths of the Middle Ages
author: Sabine Baring-Gould
query: Curious Myths of the Middle Ages Baring-Gould
epithet: Prester John, the Wandering Jew and other legends
summary: Baring-Gould's essays tracing the medieval legends — Prester John, the Wandering Jew, the Sangreal, the Man in the Moon — to their roots, a classic of Victorian comparative folklore.

title: The Fairy-Faith in Celtic Countries
author: W. Y. Evans-Wentz
query: The Fairy-Faith in Celtic Countries Evans-Wentz
epithet: Fieldwork among those who still saw fairies
summary: Evans-Wentz's Oxford thesis, gathering firsthand testimony of the fairy-faith across the Celtic lands and weighing its psychical and anthropological meaning — the classic study of the belief.

title: Celtic Folklore, Welsh and Manx
author: John Rhys
query: Celtic Folklore Welsh and Manx Rhys
epithet: The Oxford Celticist among the fairies
summary: Rhys's two-volume gathering of Welsh and Manx fairy-lore, well-lore and calendar custom — the great philologist's fieldwork, a treasury of the living Celtic supernatural.

title: Myths and Legends of the Celtic Race
author: T. W. Rolleston
query: Myths and Legends of the Celtic Race Rolleston
epithet: The gods and heroes of the Celtic world
summary: Rolleston's connected retelling and study of the Irish and Welsh mythologies — the Tuatha Dé Danann, Cú Chulainn, the Mabinogion — a standard popular gateway to Celtic myth.

title: The Gods of the Egyptians
author: E. A. Wallis Budge
query: The Gods of the Egyptians Budge
epithet: The whole pantheon of the Nile, illustrated
summary: Budge's two-volume study of Egyptian mythology and religion — the gods, the afterlife and the magical texts — the illustrated reference that fed both Egyptology and the occult imagination.

title: The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani
author: E. A. Wallis Budge
query: Book of the Dead Papyrus of Ani Budge
epithet: The funerary text of the Nile, Englished
summary: Budge's edition and translation of the Papyrus of Ani — the spells that carried the Egyptian dead through the judgement of Osiris — the version through which the modern world met the Book of the Dead.

title: A Handbook of Egyptian Religion
author: Adolf Erman
query: Handbook of Egyptian Religion Erman
epithet: The critical philologist's Egyptian religion
summary: Erman's concise, rigorous handbook of the religion of ancient Egypt — the sober German philological counterweight to Budge, tracing the gods, cult and afterlife through the texts.

title: Hauptprobleme der Gnosis
author: Wilhelm Bousset
query: Hauptprobleme der Gnosis Bousset
epithet: The chief problems of Gnostic origins
summary: Bousset's study of the central problems of Gnosticism, tracing its motifs to Iranian and Babylonian religion — a landmark of the history-of-religions school and of the study of ancient Gnosis.

title: Les Grands Initiés
author: Édouard Schuré
query: Les Grands Inities Schure
epithet: The chain of the great initiates of history
summary: Schuré's hugely popular romance of the 'great initiates' — Rama, Krishna, Hermes, Moses, Orpheus, Pythagoras, Plato, Jesus — the book that fixed the perennialist image of a single hidden wisdom.

title: Atlantis: The Antediluvian World
author: Ignatius Donnelly
query: Atlantis The Antediluvian World Donnelly
epithet: The book that founded modern Atlantis lore
summary: Donnelly's argument that Plato's Atlantis was a real sunken civilisation, the mother of all cultures — the fountainhead of a century and a half of Atlantis speculation and 'rejected knowledge'.

title: Anacalypsis
author: Godfrey Higgins
query: Anacalypsis Higgins Saitic Isis
epithet: An attempt to unveil the one universal religion
summary: Higgins's enormous, eccentric attempt to trace all religions and mythologies to a single lost universal source — a monument of nineteenth-century esoteric scholarship and a favourite of the occult revival.

title: A Discourse on the Worship of Priapus
author: Richard Payne Knight
query: Discourse on the Worship of Priapus Knight
epithet: The scandalous study of phallic religion
summary: Knight's notorious inquiry into the phallic symbolism he found running through the mythology and religion of the ancient world — a founding, much-suppressed text of the comparative study of sexual religion.

title: A New System, or an Analysis of Ancient Mythology
author: Jacob Bryant
query: New System Analysis of Ancient Mythology Bryant
epithet: All myth traced back to the Flood and Noah
summary: Bryant's vast attempt to reduce the whole of pagan mythology to a corrupted memory of the Flood and the family of Noah — the eighteenth century's grandest syncretic mythography.

title: A Book of the Beginnings
author: Gerald Massey
query: A Book of the Beginnings Massey
epithet: All civilisation traced to Egypt
summary: Massey's two-volume argument that Egypt is the origin of the world's myths, language and religion — a monument of self-taught Egyptological speculation that shaped Afrocentric and esoteric thought.

title: Ancient Faiths Embodied in Ancient Names
author: Thomas Inman
query: Ancient Faiths Embodied in Ancient Names Inman
epithet: The hidden sexual religion in sacred names
summary: Inman's two-volume decoding of divine names and religious symbols as disguised sexual and solar worship — a widely read Victorian work of comparative symbolism and 'phallicism'.

title: The Physical Phenomena of Spiritualism
author: Hereward Carrington
query: Physical Phenomena of Spiritualism Carrington
epithet: Fraudulent, doubtful and genuine, sorted
summary: Carrington's systematic examination of the physical phenomena of the séance — the tricks of fraudulent mediums exposed alongside the residue he judged genuine — a standard of critical psychical research.

title: Phenomena of Materialisation
author: Albert von Schrenck-Notzing
query: Phenomena of Materialisation Schrenck-Notzing
epithet: The photographic study of ectoplasm
summary: Schrenck-Notzing's heavily photographed laboratory study of the 'materialisations' and ectoplasm of his mediums — the most notorious attempt to document physical mediumship as a science.

title: Cock Lane and Common-Sense
author: Andrew Lang
query: Cock Lane and Common-Sense Lang
epithet: Ghost-stories weighed by an anthropologist
summary: Lang's witty study of hauntings, poltergeists and second sight across history, arguing that such reports are a constant of human experience deserving the anthropologist's attention.

title: The Legend of Perseus
author: Edwin Sidney Hartland
query: The Legend of Perseus Hartland
epithet: One myth pursued through all its folklore
summary: Hartland's three-volume study following the motifs of the Perseus story — the supernatural birth, the life-token, the slaying — through the folklore of the whole world; a monument of the comparative method.

title: Etruscan Roman Remains in Popular Tradition
author: Charles Godfrey Leland
query: Etruscan Roman Remains in Popular Tradition Leland
epithet: A surviving witch-religion in the Romagna
summary: Leland's collection of the spells, gods and witch-lore he claimed to have found still alive among the peasants of Tuscany — the fieldwork behind Aradia and a key source for the witch-cult theory.

title: History of European Morals from Augustus to Charlemagne
author: W. E. H. Lecky
query: History of European Morals Lecky
epithet: The moral history that framed magic and miracle
summary: Lecky's history of the moral development of Europe, whose treatment of magic, miracle and the decline of the belief in the marvellous is a classic statement of the rationalist reading of the past.

title: The Belief in Immortality and the Worship of the Dead
author: James George Frazer
query: Belief in Immortality and the Worship of the Dead Frazer
epithet: Frazer's Gifford Lectures on the cult of the dead
summary: Frazer's Gifford Lectures surveying the belief in immortality and the propitiation of the dead across the world's peoples — a major late statement of his comparative anthropology of religion.

title: Magic in Names and in Other Things
author: Edward Clodd
query: Magic in Names and in Other Things Clodd
epithet: The power of the name across the world
summary: Clodd's study of the widespread belief in the magical power of names, words and things — a readable synthesis of the folklore of word-magic by a leading popular anthropologist.

title: Magic and Fetishism
author: A. C. Haddon
query: Magic and Fetishism Haddon
epithet: A short anthropology of the magical object
summary: Haddon's compact study of magic, fetish and taboo from the anthropologist's standpoint — a clear little handbook of the primitive uses of the uncanny by a founder of British field anthropology.

title: Ritual and Belief
author: Edwin Sidney Hartland
query: Ritual and Belief Hartland
epithet: Studies in the anthropology of religion
summary: Hartland's essays on the relation of rite and belief among primitive peoples — myth, magic, oath and taboo — a mature statement of the English folklore school's approach to religion.

title: Queen Móo and the Egyptian Sphinx
author: Augustus Le Plongeon
query: Queen Moo and the Egyptian Sphinx Le Plongeon
epithet: The Maya as the mother of Egypt and Atlantis
summary: Le Plongeon's argument that Maya civilisation was the source of Egypt, Atlantis and the mysteries — pioneering, wildly speculative diffusionism that became a staple of esoteric prehistory.

title: The Problem of Atlantis
author: Lewis Spence
query: The Problem of Atlantis Spence
epithet: A folklorist argues the case for Atlantis
summary: Spence's attempt to make a scholarly case for a sunken Atlantic continent from geology, folklore and diffusion — the most respectable twentieth-century restatement of the Atlantis hypothesis.

title: The Book of Ceremonial Magic (Black Magic and Pacts)
author: Arthur Edward Waite
query: Book of Black Magic and of Pacts Waite
epithet: A critical anatomy of the grimoire literature
summary: Waite's critical survey and partial exposure of the literature of ceremonial magic and the pacts with spirits — an early scholarly attempt to map the grimoire tradition, sceptical of its claims.

title: Ethnology in Folklore
author: George Laurence Gomme
query: Ethnology in Folklore Gomme
epithet: Reading prehistory out of surviving custom
summary: Gomme's argument that the customs and superstitions of the modern peasantry preserve the beliefs of prehistoric races — a programmatic statement of the 'survivals' method at the heart of Victorian folklore.

title: The Science of Fairy Tales
author: Edwin Sidney Hartland
query: The Science of Fairy Tales Hartland
epithet: An inquiry into fairy mythology
summary: Hartland's comparative study of the fairy tale — changelings, the supernatural lapse of time, the fairy midwife — a founding work of the anthropological study of folk narrative.

title: Introduction to the Science of Religion
author: F. Max Müller
query: Introduction to the Science of Religion Max Muller
epithet: The founding manifesto of comparative religion
summary: Max Müller's lectures proposing the comparative 'science of religion' and his theory of myth as a 'disease of language' — the book that named and launched the academic study of religion.

title: The Tibetan Book of the Dead
author: W. Y. Evans-Wentz (ed.)
query: Tibetan Book of the Dead Evans-Wentz Bardo Thodol
epithet: The Bardo Thödol brought to the West
summary: Evans-Wentz's edition of the Bardo Thödol — the Tibetan guide to the states between death and rebirth — the book that carried Tibetan Buddhism into Western esotericism and, later, to Jung.

title: The Real History of the Rosicrucians
author: Arthur Edward Waite
query: Real History of the Rosicrucians Waite
epithet: The first sober history of the Rose Cross
summary: Waite's attempt at a documentary history of the Rosicrucians from the manifestos onward — sceptical of the legends, and the starting point for the modern scholarly study of the movement.

title: Aspects of Religious Belief and Practice in Babylonia and Assyria
author: Morris Jastrow
query: Religious Belief and Practice in Babylonia and Assyria Jastrow
epithet: The divination and magic of Mesopotamia
summary: Jastrow's study of Babylonian and Assyrian religion, with its rich treatment of omens, astrology and divination — a standard account of the Mesopotamian roots of Western astral magic.
imprint: New York: G. P. Putnam's Sons, 1911

title: The Cults of the Greek States
author: Lewis Richard Farnell
query: The Cults of the Greek States Farnell
epithet: The definitive survey of Greek cult
summary: Farnell's five-volume survey of the cults, rites and mysteries of the Greek gods — the exhaustive reference on ancient Greek religion, including its mystery-cults and chthonic worship.

title: Germanic Origins: A Study in Primitive Culture
author: Francis Barton Gummere
query: Germanic Origins Study in Primitive Culture Gummere
epithet: The heathen roots of the Germanic world
summary: Gummere's study of the primitive Germanic culture — its heathen belief, magic and custom — reconstructed from language and early literature, a source-book for the pagan background of the North.

title: The Religion of the Ancient Celts
author: J. A. MacCulloch
query: The Religion of the Ancient Celts MacCulloch
epithet: The gods, druids and cult of the Celts
summary: MacCulloch's comprehensive study of Celtic religion — the gods, the druids, sacrifice, the cult of the dead and the otherworld — the standard scholarly account for a generation.

title: The Melanesians of British New Guinea
author: C. G. Seligman
query: The Melanesians of British New Guinea Seligman
epithet: Sorcery and magic in Melanesian life
summary: Seligman's ethnography of British New Guinea, a foundational field-study whose detailed record of sorcery, magic and the dead shaped the anthropological understanding of the magical worldview.

title: The Malleus Maleficarum
author: Heinrich Kramer, trans. Montague Summers
query: Malleus Maleficarum Summers translation
epithet: The witch-hunters' manual, Englished at last
summary: Summers's English translation of the Malleus Maleficarum, the fifteenth-century inquisitors' manual for detecting and destroying witches — the single most notorious text of the witch-hunts.

title: A History of the Inquisition of Spain
author: Henry Charles Lea
query: History of the Inquisition of Spain Lea
epithet: The archival history of the Spanish tribunal
summary: Lea's four-volume history of the Spanish Inquisition, built from the archives — its procedures, its victims and its pursuit of sorcery and heresy — the standard critical account.

title: Narratives of Sorcery and Magic
author: Thomas Wright
query: Narratives of Sorcery and Magic Wright
epithet: A Victorian history from the trial records
summary: Wright's two-volume history of sorcery and magic told through its famous cases — a readable Victorian narrative drawn from the trial records of the whole European tradition.

title: The History of the Supernatural
author: William Howitt
query: The History of the Supernatural Howitt
epithet: Two volumes of the marvellous across all ages
summary: Howitt's two-volume survey of supernatural belief and experience across the nations and ages, marshalled to argue that the spiritual phenomena of his own day were no novelty.

title: Custom and Myth
author: Andrew Lang
query: Custom and Myth Andrew Lang
epithet: The comparative method against solar mythology
summary: Lang's essays applying the anthropological comparative method to myth and custom — the collection that broke the grip of Max Müller's solar mythology on English folklore.

title: Totemism and Exogamy
author: James George Frazer
query: Totemism and Exogamy Frazer
epithet: The comparative anatomy of the totem-clan
summary: Frazer's four-volume survey of totemism and marriage-rules among the peoples of the world — the vast comparative compendium behind his theory of the origins of religion and society.

title: An Introduction to the History of Religion
author: Frank Byron Jevons
query: An Introduction to the History of Religion Jevons
epithet: Magic, taboo and totem in one primer
summary: Jevons's textbook of the origins of religion — mana, taboo, totemism, sacrifice and magic — the widely used primer that carried the Frazerian anthropology of religion to students.

title: Irish Witchcraft and Demonology
author: St John D. Seymour
query: Irish Witchcraft and Demonology Seymour
epithet: The witch trials of Ireland collected
summary: Seymour's history of witchcraft and demonology in Ireland, gathering its scattered trials and hauntings — the standard account of a national tradition little studied before.

title: The Devil in Britain and America
author: John Ashton
query: The Devil in Britain and America Ashton
epithet: A popular history of the Fiend and his witches
summary: Ashton's illustrated popular history of the Devil, witchcraft and possession in Britain and America — a genial Victorian gathering of the whole demonological tradition.

title: Tom Tit Tot: An Essay on Savage Philosophy in Folk-Tale
author: Edward Clodd
query: Tom Tit Tot Clodd savage philosophy
epithet: The power of the name in the fairy-tale
summary: Clodd's study of the name-magic at the heart of the Rumpelstiltskin tale, tracing the belief in the power of the secret name through the folklore of the world.
